profile.reading: This is QGEN01, a data center at Via Isonzo 21 in Genoa, Italy, developed by Quadrivium Digital, a carrier neutral data center and subsea cable landing infrastructure company founded in 2022 and headquartered in London, United Kingdom. Quadrivium acquired the site, formerly a Banca Carige data center, in June 2022, and formally announced the redevelopment project in September 2024. The building spans about 9,000 square meters, or roughly 96,900 square feet, offering about 12 megawatts of IT power, engineered to Tier IV resilience standards for its power feed entry, or PFE, area handling subsea cable landing infrastructure, and Tier III plus resilience for its interconnection and general IT workload areas. Quadrivium markets the site as Genoas first purpose built, carrier neutral hub, providing cable landing as a service capable of supporting up to 8 submarine cable systems through a marine borepipe and beach landing at nearby Sturla beach, alongside colocation, interconnection, and two international internet exchange points, positioning Genoa as a new Mediterranean gateway for Europe, Asia, and Africa traffic alongside more established hubs such as Marseille and Frankfurt. Italian fiber and colocation operator Retelit has partnered with Quadrivium to launch a strategic point of presence at the site. Full operational status was originally targeted for the fourth quarter of 2025 but had slipped to a summer 2026 target as of sourcing checked this session.

reading.body:
Quadrivium QGEN01 in Genoa offers 12 megawatts of IT capacity and direct subsea cable landing infrastructure, positioning the Mediterranean as an emerging AI traffic hub alongside Paris and Frankfurt.

The facility spans 9,000 square meters in a repurposed bank data center, engineered to Tier IV standards for its cable landing area and Tier III-plus for general colocation. Quadrivium designed it to terminate up to 8 submarine cables through a marine landing at nearby Sturla beach, making it a cable landing service rather than a traditional colocation-only site. This infrastructure class matters for AI because large model inference and training require not just power and floor space, but direct international connectivity with the low-latency, high-bandwidth characteristics that cable landing stations provide.

The site's geographic position reflects a deliberate regional strategy. Genoa sits on a Mediterranean route connecting Europe to Asia and Africa, filling a gap between established hubs. Retelit's partnership to operate a point of presence there signals confidence that Mediterranean AI traffic will justify the infrastructure investment. The slip from Q4 2025 to summer 2026 operational status indicates the typical delays in purpose-built facilities of this type, particularly when integrating subsea cable infrastructure.

The data does not specify what drove Quadrivium's acquisition of the Banca Carige building, why this particular beach location was chosen for cable landing, or what power source will feed the 12 megawatts. It also does not indicate whether this facility will serve local colocation demand or primarily function as a cable hub for traffic transiting the region.
